questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses, a very different cultural experience, nature, interesting city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: One orientation event and then option to pay for tours of the city and other social activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Me and a friend found housing two months in advance through Facebook. However, I can strongly recommend housing through "simple spaces"! make sure to rent a room as early as possible as it is popular.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I can't recommend living in Goshitels (a specific type of small apartment) from what I've heard from others - very small and crammed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found that it could be difficult to keep on top of the different deadlines - I was constantly afraid that I might have missed one.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A designated person to email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of them besides one that had only few spots

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: read all mails very well and put deadlines in a calendar.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the academic level in the designated "Study Abroad" classes too easy. I loved the course "Ecological Anthropology". I had one graduate course, and I would probably check with the professor beforehand how much time should be allocated to the course since I had to do a to of work for mine.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had four BA courses and one MA course. I found the academic level in the designated "Study Abroad" classes too easy. I loved the course "Ecological Anthropology". I had one graduate course, and I would probably check with the professor beforehand how much time should be allocated to the course since I had to do a to of work for mine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It varied a lot from class to class. not something I thought about.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Ecological Anthropology, Postcolonialisms, Contemporary Korean Cinema and Society, Society and Human Behavior, Introduction to Korean Philosophy.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I strongly recommend Ecological Anthropology! The best structured classes, the academic level was perfect and the professor is very engaged. I went on a field trip over a weekend with this class. And it was such interesting topics in my opinion.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Not something I thought about. It was cheaper than Denmark generally about 2/3 of Danish prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A mentoring program where you are put in a group with other exchange students. there were also sports clubs, but I found this difficult to engage with due to language barriers. Also big Game days.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It can be nice to have the mentor group, I however did not use it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips and see rest of South Korea! I recommend Simple Spaces's group trips as a good way to meet people and have some experiences you might not on your own trips. Name island is beautiful (especially during fall). Seocho is a nice city. I also recommend hiking the mountains inside Seoul, they are all very available.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some weeks for me, but I think this was also due to the high temperatures the first month of my stay. The city is so big, so I recommend getting local in some of the areas to feel at home faster rather than wanting to see everything at once.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: This was difficult at Yonsei since I didn't really have classes with local students. But I think joining some of the student groups is a good idea. I can really recommend the app Bumble BFF to find local friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barrier was probably most difficult. people keep a lot to themselves, but this is very similar to Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everywhere in Seoul is interesting in some sort of way - there is always something fun og different to look at or experience. It's also a very welcoming and safe culture - I never felt unsafe

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a lot (too many) Americans. Use the Business building to study in, it is pretty. Enjoy the beautiful campus:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: In all honesty I would choose SKKU rather than Yonsei if I could do it differently. But overall my exchange at Yonsei was pleasant.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many new people and learning that I can feel at home in a completely different culture. I really really recommend exchange in Seoul!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting friends at the university

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
